title: Bias in Large Language Models Across Clinical Applications: A Systematic Review

bias_targets.methodology: Systematic review of studies measuring racial and ethnic disparities using methods such as clinical vignettes, demographic analysis of AI-generated medical images (e.g., skin tones, physician representation), differences in diagnostic or treatment recommendations, and reading grade level analysis of clinical outputs.

Systematic review of studies evaluating gender bias through demographic profiling of AI-generated images of healthcare professionals, linguistic text analysis of AI-generated letters of recommendation (comparing male vs. female names/pronouns), and analyzing differential treatment plans in clinical vignettes.

Systematic review of studies that assessed age-related bias by analyzing the demographic tailoring of symptom checker recommendations and evaluating age representation in AI-generated images of medical professionals.

Systematic review of studies examining socioeconomic bias by comparing model outputs for clinical vignettes involving different socioeconomic statuses and calculating polarity/subjectivity scores of discharge instructions across different patient insurance types.

Systematic review of studies identifying disability bias through linguistic analysis of generated descriptions of people with and without disabilities, parsing words into favorable or limiting qualities.

Systematic review of studies assessing language bias by comparing diagnostic accuracy, correct response rates, and efficiency scores across different languages (e.g., English versus Chinese medical licensing examinations).

Systematic review of studies evaluating bias based on specific health behaviors, such as measuring whether models prioritize acoustic data-driven predictions over a patient's self-reported smoking status.
